control_failures.control_label: emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment

facts.hazard_release: fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation
facts.title: potential incident during a breakdown response on P-7111

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control EMERGENCY_ISOLATION_ON_RELEASE: the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective, and the ICAM investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

recommendations: Confirm at the next critical control verification that the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment on P-7111, PT-7111 and TK-7102 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in maintaining sealing systems on rotating equipment, specifically replacing seals and seal support fluid. P-7111 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during a breakdown response while the emergency isolation and depressuring on loss of containment was never verified as effective. The chemical energy involved is held as hydrocarbon, and the recorded presentation was fire, toxic exposure, corrosive contact, detonation.
response.summary: On 4 March 2016 a potential incident was recorded on P-7111, PT-7111 and TK-7102 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during a breakdown response; chemical energy held as hydrocarbon was not released.
